result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.cmty_fast_label_propagation()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find communities with fast label propagation. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L30439-L30506){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.cmty_fast_label_propagation( weighted=None, seed=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Fast label propagation communities](/assets/graphs/cmty-fast-label-propagation.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense four-node groups, A, B, C, D and E, F, G, H, joined by the single edge D to E. Every node starts with its own label and adopts its neighbors' most common label, revisiting only nodes whose neighborhood changed; with seed 1 the labels settle on the two groups, drawn in the accent color and teal. The card lists community 0 as A, B, C, D and community 1 as E, F, G, H." width="100%"} Label propagation lets every node adopt the label most common among its neighbors until labels stabilize into communities. The fast variant (Traag and Šubelj, 2023) keeps a queue of nodes whose neighborhood just changed and only revisits those, which makes it several times faster than sweeping over all nodes while finding communities of similar quality. It suits very large graphs where a quick, parameter-free partition is wanted. Edge direction is ignored. Ties between labels are broken at random; use `seed=` for reproducible results. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether neighbors vote with their edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the communities in (default `"cmty_fast_label_propagation"`). [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the node-to-community dictionary instead of storing it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : With `return_dict=True`, a dictionary mapping node IDs to community labels (numbered in order of the lowest node ID in each); otherwise `self`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Nodes start with distinct labels and are queued in random order; a dequeued node takes a label of maximal (weighted) frequency among its neighbors, and if its label changed, its neighbors with other labels are queued again. The process ends when the queue empties. Follows NetworkX's `fast_label_propagation_communities`; with a different random generator, the result for a given seed differs. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#5eef62ba .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(list("ABCDEFGH")) g.add_edges( [("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("B", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D"), ("E", "F"), ("E", "G"), ("E", "H"), ("F", "G"), ("F", "H"), ("G", "H"), ("D", "E")] ) len(set(g.cmty_fast_label_propagation(seed=1, return_dict=True).values())) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
